paths.question: Is this material metallic?
paths.establishes: Whether the accepted reference state has occupied and empty states meeting the Fermi level across the full Brillouin zone.

gates.title: Accept the electronic reference state
gates.required_evidence: A converged, physically identified charge and magnetic state.
gates.pass: The reference state and occupations are reproducible under the declared setup.
gates.stop: SCF convergence, occupations, or the physical state remain ambiguous.

gates.title: Resolve states near the Fermi level
gates.required_evidence: A converged DOS with enough energy and k-space resolution near EF.
gates.pass: Finite or vanishing spectral weight near EF is numerically resolved.
gates.stop: Broadening or sampling can change the classification.

gates.title: Establish the full-zone occupation boundary
gates.required_evidence: Full-BZ eigenvalues or a validated dense interpolation.
gates.pass: All pockets crossing EF are located and stable to mesh refinement.
gates.stop: Only a presentation band path has been inspected.

gates.title: Use the band path as context
gates.required_evidence: A symmetry-labelled path calculated from the same accepted reference.
gates.pass: The path explains dispersions without being used as the sole metallicity test.
gates.stop: The band-path crossing is being treated as full-BZ proof.

gates.title: Validate the metallicity claim
gates.required_evidence: DOS and full-BZ evidence agree within declared numerical sensitivity.
gates.pass: The claim names the reference state, sampling and observable.
gates.stop: Different observables or reference states disagree without explanation.

claim_boundary: A high-symmetry band crossing alone does not prove full-BZ metallicity.
Metallicity does not establish superconductivity, transport quality, or a pairing mechanism.

paths.question: Is this structure dynamically stable?
paths.establishes: Whether an accepted structure is a harmonic local minimum for the sampled collective displacements across the Brillouin zone.

gates.title: Accept the relaxed structure
gates.required_evidence: Forces, stress, constraints, cell and identity are accepted.
gates.pass: The geometry is stationary to target-relevant tolerances.
gates.stop: Residual force, stress, symmetry or identity is unresolved.

gates.title: Accept the electronic reference
gates.required_evidence: Stable SCF and occupations for the relaxed geometry.
gates.pass: Force constants will be derivatives of a reproducible state.
gates.stop: Electronic noise can change shallow force constants.

gates.title: Use Γ as a diagnostic
gates.required_evidence: Γ modes, eigenvectors and acoustic behavior.
gates.pass: Cell-periodic modes are interpretable and acoustic artifacts are bounded.
gates.stop: A Γ-only result is being generalized to the full zone.

gates.title: Check the full q-space model
gates.required_evidence: A converged q mesh or real-space force-constant range covering the BZ.
gates.pass: No robust negative eigenvalue remains in the declared harmonic model.
gates.stop: An instability persists away from Γ or moves with convergence controls.

gates.title: Interpret acoustic and flexural modes
gates.required_evidence: Stress, vacuum, rotational/acoustic constraints and long-wavelength behavior.
gates.pass: A shallow ZA feature is separated from a robust downhill mode.
gates.stop: A 2D Γ artifact and a physical instability cannot be distinguished.

gates.title: State the harmonic boundary
gates.required_evidence: Anharmonic or finite-temperature evidence when the claim requires it.
gates.pass: The conclusion is explicitly local and harmonic, or supported beyond it.
gates.stop: Harmonic stability is being used as thermodynamic or synthetic proof.

claim_boundary: No imaginary harmonic mode supports only local harmonic stability of the declared model.
It does not prove global thermodynamic stability, kinetic accessibility, or synthesizability.

paths.question: Does this material support phonon-mediated superconductivity?
paths.establishes: A gated evidence chain from a valid structure and electronic phase through phonons, electron–phonon coupling and a bounded Tc model.

gates.title: Accept structure and phase
gates.required_evidence: Accepted geometry, composition, constraints and phase identity.
gates.pass: The reference structure is numerically accepted.
gates.stop: Do not calculate downstream pairing quantities for an unaccepted structure.

gates.title: Establish full-BZ metallicity
gates.required_evidence: Resolved Fermi-surface sheets and dense low-energy states.
gates.pass: The relevant carriers and pockets are numerically stable.
gates.stop: A band path alone is the metallicity evidence.

gates.title: Resolve the magnetic reference
gates.required_evidence: Relevant magnetic and nonmagnetic states compared consistently.
gates.pass: The pairing calculation uses an identified electronic phase.
gates.stop: Competing magnetic states remain unresolved.

gates.title: Resolve SOC sensitivity
gates.required_evidence: SOC changes to pockets, degeneracies and occupations.
gates.pass: SOC is included or shown not to alter the target evidence.
gates.stop: SOC-sensitive low-energy states are treated scalar-relativistically without a bound.

gates.title: Support dynamical stability
gates.required_evidence: Converged phonons over the required q space.
gates.pass: The EPC reference has no unexplained robust unstable mode.
gates.stop: Large coupling comes from an unresolved unstable reference.

gates.title: Converge the EPC spectrum
gates.required_evidence: Dense electronic/q sampling, mode-resolved matrix elements and α²F.
gates.pass: λ, ωlog and dominant modes are stable to relevant controls.
gates.stop: A coarse mesh or broadening determines λ.

gates.title: Bound the Tc model
gates.required_evidence: Declared Coulomb model, Migdal regime, isotropy/anisotropy and sensitivity tests.
gates.pass: Tc is reported with numerical and model sensitivity.
gates.stop: A single λ or single μ* estimate is promoted to validated superconductivity.

claim_boundary: Large λ alone is not validated superconductivity.
A calculated Tc is conditional on structure, phase, phonons, Coulomb treatment and pairing approximations; experiment establishes an actual superconducting phase.

paths.question: Is an apparent imaginary phonon physical or numerical?
paths.establishes: Whether a negative harmonic eigenvalue is a reproducible downhill structural direction rather than a convergence, interpolation or invariance artifact.

gates.title: Revalidate the reference
gates.required_evidence: Forces, stress, symmetry and electronic state at the phonon geometry.
gates.pass: The phonon is evaluated at an accepted stationary reference.
gates.stop: Residual relaxation error can drive the mode.

gates.title: Converge electronic derivatives
gates.required_evidence: Tight SCF, k mesh, smearing, basis and response thresholds.
gates.pass: The eigenvalue and eigenvector survive electronic convergence.
gates.stop: The sign changes with electronic controls.

gates.title: Converge force-constant range
gates.required_evidence: q mesh or supercell, interpolation and acoustic/rotational handling.
gates.pass: The mode is stable in location and character.
gates.stop: It follows grid, interpolation or image interactions.

gates.title: Test the 2D long-wavelength limit
gates.required_evidence: ZA dispersion, residual stress, vacuum and invariance checks.
gates.pass: A Γ-near flexural artifact is bounded or corrected.
gates.stop: The long-wavelength behavior remains method-dependent.

gates.title: Follow the mode
gates.required_evidence: Displacements along ± eigenvector and structural relaxation.
gates.pass: Energy lowering and a physically interpretable distortion reproduce.
gates.stop: The mode has no stable eigenvector or energy-lowering continuation.

gates.title: Separate harmonic and finite-temperature claims
gates.required_evidence: Free-energy or finite-temperature treatment if stabilization is claimed.
gates.pass: The temperature-dependent claim has matching evidence.
gates.stop: A harmonic soft mode is dismissed solely from a short trajectory.

claim_boundary: A robust negative eigenvalue identifies a harmonic downhill direction, not automatically the final phase.
A small Γ-near ZA feature in 2D requires invariance and convergence evidence before it is called physical.

paths.question: Does spin–orbit coupling qualitatively change the low-energy physics?
paths.establishes: Whether SOC changes the relevant bands, Fermi surface, spin texture, symmetry classification or downstream observable rather than only adding a small energy correction.

gates.title: Define the scalar-relativistic reference
gates.required_evidence: A converged geometry, magnetic state and low-energy band manifold.
gates.pass: The comparison starts from the same physical reference.
gates.stop: Geometry or magnetism differs between the compared runs.

gates.title: Run a matched SOC calculation
gates.required_evidence: Fully relativistic datasets and consistent noncollinear settings.
gates.pass: The SOC result is numerically comparable to the reference.
gates.stop: Core treatment or setup changes confound the SOC difference.

gates.title: Compare low-energy topology
gates.required_evidence: Splittings, gaps, pockets and occupations over the full relevant zone.
gates.pass: Qualitative changes are located and stable to sampling.
gates.stop: Only a visual band-path difference is available.

gates.title: Resolve spin and symmetry content
gates.required_evidence: Spin texture, anisotropy or symmetry-resolved states as needed.
gates.pass: The proposed SOC mechanism appears in the target states.
gates.stop: SOC splitting is present but the claimed spin protection or texture is untested.

gates.title: Recompute the affected observable
gates.required_evidence: Matched SOC/no-SOC target calculations or a justified sensitivity bound.
gates.pass: The final claim states what SOC changes and what it does not.
gates.stop: A normal-state SOC result is promoted to superconducting or topological proof.

claim_boundary: SOC band splitting is not by itself evidence of Ising pairing or topology.
Qualitative SOC sensitivity must be evaluated for the states and observable used in the final claim.

paths.question: Is DFT+U required, and what does U actually change?
paths.establishes: Which localized subspace and observables are sensitive to U, and whether the scientific conclusion survives justified model choices.

gates.title: Define the corrected subspace
gates.required_evidence: Projectors, occupation matrix, double counting and U convention.
gates.pass: The model is reproducible and physically motivated.
gates.stop: U is quoted without its subspace and implementation.

gates.title: Compare relevant self-consistent branches
gates.required_evidence: Matched structural and magnetic candidates at each U.
gates.pass: State ordering is compared without branch switching ambiguity.
gates.stop: One initial magnetic state is treated as the ground state.

gates.title: Scan a justified U range
gates.required_evidence: Observable trends under U/projector variation or independent U estimation.
gates.pass: Robust and U-dependent conclusions are separated.
gates.stop: The conclusion exists only at one arbitrary U.

gates.title: Separate changed observables
gates.required_evidence: Gap, moment, exchange, anisotropy and structure evaluated separately.
gates.pass: Each claim is tied to its calculated object.
gates.stop: Gap opening is used as proof of magnetic order or finite-temperature Tc.

gates.title: Bound the DFT+U conclusion
gates.required_evidence: Comparison with another method or experiment where available.
gates.pass: The report states model dependence and surviving conclusions.
gates.stop: DFT+U is described as uniformly more accurate.

claim_boundary: U is part of a declared localized-subspace model, not a universal material constant.
Gap, moment, exchange, anisotropy and ordering temperature are distinct claims.

paths.question: Is a heterostructure electronically coupled or merely stacked?
paths.establishes: Whether the combined interface develops reproducible hybridization, charge redistribution or interfacial states beyond a geometric stack of isolated layers.

gates.title: Define the physical interface
gates.required_evidence: Termination, registry, strain, separation and boundary conditions.
gates.pass: The model corresponds to a stated interface hypothesis.
gates.stop: A convenient commensurate cell is treated as the unique interface.

gates.title: Accept interface geometry and energetics
gates.required_evidence: Relaxation, binding reference and relevant registries/distances.
gates.pass: The analyzed interface is a reproducible local structure.
gates.stop: Registry or separation sensitivity remains unresolved.

gates.title: Quantify charge redistribution
gates.required_evidence: A declared density-difference reference plus electrostatic checks.
gates.pass: Redistribution and net transfer are not conflated.
gates.stop: Nominal valence or a single partitioning number is the sole evidence.

gates.title: Resolve wavefunction mixing
gates.required_evidence: Layer/orbital projections, avoided crossings or bonding analysis.
gates.pass: Mixed states are identified in the combined system.
gates.stop: Layer-projected DOS alone cannot separate shift from mixing.

gates.title: Track the electrostatic reference
gates.required_evidence: Consistent vacuum/potential references and interface dipole.
gates.pass: Isolated and combined-system alignments are distinguished.
gates.stop: Isolated work functions are used as the final interface alignment.

gates.title: State the coupling mechanism
gates.required_evidence: Energetic, charge, orbital and alignment evidence agree.
gates.pass: The claim names which coupling is actually supported.
gates.stop: Stacking, charge transfer and hybridization are used as synonyms.

claim_boundary: Geometric contact or binding does not prove strong electronic hybridization.
Charge redistribution, net transfer, band alignment and wavefunction mixing require different evidence.

paths.question: Is an interface Type-I, Type-II, or Type-III?
paths.establishes: A band-edge ordering tied to a declared structural, electrostatic and electronic reference, including interface-induced changes.

gates.title: Establish component band edges
gates.required_evidence: Comparable band edges with adequate functional/SOC treatment.
gates.pass: Component uncertainties are smaller than the proposed ordering.
gates.stop: Functional or SOC sensitivity can reverse the alignment.

gates.title: Align electrostatic references
gates.required_evidence: Vacuum level, macroscopic potential or an explicit common reference.
gates.pass: Offsets are computed in a common convention.
gates.stop: Independent eigenvalues are compared without an alignment reference.

gates.title: Relax and calculate the combined interface
gates.required_evidence: Accepted registry, strain, distance and combined electronic state.
gates.pass: The final classification belongs to the actual interface model.
gates.stop: Only isolated-component Anderson alignment is available.

gates.title: Check dipoles and hybridization
gates.required_evidence: Interface dipole, redistributed charge and layer/orbital states.
gates.pass: Band-edge identity survives or its reconstruction is explained.
gates.stop: Hybridization makes component band labels ill-defined.

gates.title: Bound the alignment label
gates.required_evidence: Offsets and uncertainties support I, II or broken-gap III ordering.
gates.pass: The classification names structure, method and reference.
gates.stop: Near-degenerate offsets are reported as a categorical type.

claim_boundary: An isolated-component lineup is a starting model, not the final interface classification.
A categorical type requires offsets larger than the relevant numerical and model uncertainty.

paths.question: Does intercalation cause a meaningful electronic transition?
paths.establishes: Whether an identified guest concentration and structure produce a reproducible change in electronic phase rather than an uncontrolled mixture of charge, strain, defects and kinetics.

gates.title: Identify guest content and host phase
gates.required_evidence: Stoichiometry, sites, staging and host structural identity.
gates.pass: The before/after states are chemically and structurally defined.
gates.stop: Nominal exposure is the only concentration evidence.

gates.title: Compare accessible structures
gates.required_evidence: Competing host/guest configurations and relaxation.
gates.pass: The electronic comparison is made between accepted structures.
gates.stop: Charge doping and structural reconstruction are conflated.

gates.title: Resolve access pathways
gates.required_evidence: Edge, top-surface, defect or interlayer pathways as relevant.
gates.pass: The proposed state is kinetically reachable under the declared conditions.
gates.stop: A thermodynamic structure is assumed accessible without pathway evidence.

gates.title: Establish the electronic change
gates.required_evidence: Carrier count, pockets, orbital states and matched controls.
gates.pass: A phase-relevant electronic reconstruction is resolved.
gates.stop: A rigid-band or jellium proxy is treated as the full intercalated material.

gates.title: Connect to measured evidence
gates.required_evidence: Spectroscopy, diffraction, microscopy, Hall or transport matched to the claim.
gates.pass: Charge, structure and observable changes form a bounded chain.
gates.stop: Correlation with exposure time is presented as a unique mechanism.

gates.title: Test reversibility separately
gates.required_evidence: Removal cycles or reversible pathway evidence when claimed.
gates.pass: Reversibility is directly observed or not claimed.
gates.stop: A before/after experiment is called reversible without a return path.

claim_boundary: Nominal stoichiometry is not measured carrier density.
Intercalation changes charge, structure, defects and kinetics together; a meaningful transition must separate the causal evidence.

paths.question: Is the reported magnetic ground state robust?
paths.establishes: Whether a declared magnetic configuration remains lowest among a physically adequate candidate set under numerical, structural, SOC and interaction-model sensitivity.

gates.title: Accept structural candidates
gates.required_evidence: Matched relaxations or a justified common geometry.
gates.pass: Magnetic energies are not dominated by inconsistent structures.
gates.stop: Different magnetic states use incomparable geometry constraints.

gates.title: Search an adequate magnetic set
gates.required_evidence: Relevant ferro-, antiferro-, noncollinear or spin-spiral candidates.
gates.pass: The reported state wins within a stated candidate space.
gates.stop: One initialized state is called the ground state.

gates.title: Resolve small energy differences
gates.required_evidence: Matched basis, k mesh, thresholds and finite-size controls.
gates.pass: Ordering exceeds controlled numerical uncertainty.
gates.stop: Energy differences are comparable to convergence noise.

gates.title: Test interaction-model sensitivity
gates.required_evidence: Functional/U/projector sensitivity where localized states matter.
gates.pass: Robust and model-dependent orderings are separated.
gates.stop: The ordering reverses without a resolved model choice.

gates.title: Include anisotropy and SOC
gates.required_evidence: Anisotropy, DMI or SOC terms required by dimensionality/symmetry.
gates.pass: The orientation and low-dimensional stability have a physical scale.
gates.stop: An isotropic 2D spin model is assigned finite-temperature order without anisotropy.

gates.title: Bound the reduced spin model
gates.required_evidence: Exchange mapping residuals, candidate completeness and temperature method.
gates.pass: Ground-state, exchange and ordering-temperature claims remain distinct.
gates.stop: A fitted J or mean-field temperature is treated as independent validation.

claim_boundary: A converged magnetic solution is not automatically the global magnetic ground state.
State ordering, exchange parameters, anisotropy and finite-temperature order are separate claims.

paths.question: Is a structural energy ordering numerically meaningful?
paths.establishes: Whether the energy hierarchy of competing structures exceeds numerical and model uncertainty under comparable constraints and identities.

gates.title: Define comparable structures
gates.required_evidence: Composition, cell, symmetry, magnetic state and constraints.
gates.pass: Each candidate represents the same thermodynamic comparison.
gates.stop: Different stoichiometries or constraints are ranked as one energy set.

gates.title: Relax each candidate consistently
gates.required_evidence: Matched force/stress criteria and relevant degrees of freedom.
gates.pass: Each energy belongs to an accepted local minimum or declared stationary point.
gates.stop: Residual forces or constrained cells bias the ordering.

gates.title: Resolve the energy scale
gates.required_evidence: Per-atom or per-formula-unit differences stable to all shared controls.
gates.pass: The ordering exceeds a demonstrated numerical uncertainty.
gates.stop: The gap is comparable to basis, k-mesh or SCF error.

gates.title: Test physical-model sensitivity
gates.required_evidence: Functional, dispersion, U, SOC or magnetic sensitivity as relevant.
gates.pass: Robust and method-dependent rankings are separated.
gates.stop: One approximation uniquely determines a near-degenerate order.

gates.title: Use the correct thermodynamic potential
gates.required_evidence: Energy, enthalpy or constrained-strain comparison matched to conditions.
gates.pass: The ordering is reported at a declared pressure/strain and reference.
gates.stop: Zero-pressure energy is used for a finite-pressure claim.

gates.title: Separate ranking from accessibility
gates.required_evidence: Barriers, phonons or synthesis evidence when accessibility is claimed.
gates.pass: The result is a bounded energetic ranking.
gates.stop: Lowest computed energy is promoted to observed or synthesizable phase.

claim_boundary: A small total-energy difference is meaningful only after numerical and model uncertainties are smaller than that difference.
Energetic ordering does not establish dynamical stability, kinetic access, or experimental realization.

paths.question: Can this band structure support a topological claim?
paths.establishes: Whether a properly identified occupied subspace, symmetry and gap carry a computed invariant with matching boundary-state evidence where required.

gates.title: Accept the electronic phase
gates.required_evidence: Structure, magnetism, filling and SOC convention are fixed.
gates.pass: The occupied subspace belongs to an identified physical phase.
gates.stop: Magnetic or structural identity remains ambiguous.

gates.title: Establish the relevant gap
gates.required_evidence: Full-BZ direct/indirect gap and filling under adequate sampling.
gates.pass: The invariant's required gap or nodal condition is resolved.
gates.stop: A band-path inversion is the only gap evidence.

gates.title: Identify protecting symmetry
gates.required_evidence: Space, magnetic and time-reversal symmetry of the computed state.
gates.pass: The claimed classification uses a symmetry actually present.
gates.stop: A symmetry indicator is applied after the symmetry is broken.

gates.title: Compute the invariant
gates.required_evidence: Wilson loop, Chern/Z2 or appropriate invariant with mesh/gauge checks.
gates.pass: The invariant is stable to discretization and subspace choices.
gates.stop: Orbital inversion or Berry curvature alone substitutes for the invariant.

gates.title: Validate any reduced representation
gates.required_evidence: Wannier/interpolation fidelity over the target energy and k range.
gates.pass: The reduced model reproduces the first-principles bands and topology.
gates.stop: Window or disentanglement choices change the classification.

gates.title: Check boundary or observable consequences
gates.required_evidence: Surface/edge states or a clearly stated reason they are not required.
gates.pass: Bulk and boundary evidence are mutually consistent.
gates.stop: A normal-state topology result is promoted to topological superconductivity or device performance.

claim_boundary: Band inversion, orbital character or SOC splitting alone is not a topological invariant.
Normal-state topology does not establish topological superconductivity, Majorana modes, or protected transport.
